snapshot.stmt: For the common envelopes defining \(\mathfrak P_T\), the existing derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply the nonprimitive upper bounds \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P[\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}]\le C(r_T+\delta_T)\). The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, and bounded-IPW martingale concentration gives \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply by a quantitative inverse-function argument that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it lies at distance \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it belongs to \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), \(G_T(\widehat\theta_T)=0\) on \(E_T\), and the fallback \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\) occurs only on a uniformly negligible event. With \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), the exact-root linearization is \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)\), and \((\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*),J,T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T)\) converges stably relative to \(\sigma(J)\) to \((-V_J^{1/2}Z,J,\Omega_J)\). If \(c^\top V_jc\) differs across two positive-mass basins, the unconditional limit of \(c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\) is a non-Gaussian centered normal scale mixture.

defs.def:basin-covariance: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).
defs.def:finite-attractor-class: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\).
defs.def:ipw-z-estimator: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).
defs.def:stable-limit-criterion: The convergence \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\to_{\mathrm{st}}-V_J^{1/2}Z\) relative to \(\sigma(J)\) means \(E_P[h(J)f(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*))]\to E_P[h(J)f(-V_J^{1/2}Z)]\) for every bounded measurable \(h\) and bounded continuous \(f\); uniformity over \(\mathfrak P_T\) means the corresponding supremum discrepancy tends to zero for unit-bounded Lipschitz \(f\) and unit-bounded \(h\).

assumptions.ass:iid-full-data: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-randomization: Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-overlap: For every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), context, and realized history, \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\).
assumptions.ass:bounded-score: The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:smooth-z-map: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
assumptions.ass:policy-lipschitz: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
assumptions.ass:finite-tail-selection: There is a tail variable \(J\in\mathcal J\), measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge1}\), such that \(\eta_t\to\bar\eta_J\) almost surely under \(P\).
assumptions.ass:vanishing-modulus: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).
assumptions.ass:basin-nondegeneracy: The basin covariances satisfy \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).

snapshot.stmt: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, \(\widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). This uniform statement strictly strengthens Saco's pointwise realized-QV pivot on the conditional finite-attractor class by deriving the variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the common attraction and exact-root localization controls.

defs.def:event-truncated-rqv-sandwich: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).
defs.def:realized-qv-pivot: For nonzero \(c\), define \(T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)/\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_Tc}\).

snapshot.stmt: Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic \(\Sigma\). Under the stable limit in Theorem 1 with \(p_j>0\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}P\{\tau\in C_T^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). The necessity is an equality-of-laws result for the finite centered Gaussian scale mixture, not a variance-matching argument at one nominal level.

A single deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). Equivalently, \(V_J\) is almost surely deterministic. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.

For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.

defs.def:basin-covariance: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).
defs.def:directional-matrix-witness: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, and put \(\eta_t=\bar\eta_J=J-1\) for every \(t\ge1\).

snapshot.stmt: For the augmented compact Markov chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\in\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\) generated by the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion, with initial slopes \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\), initialization \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\), and law \(P_{\eta_0}\), characterize the almost-sure limit set of the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\). In particular, determine whether there exist \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\ge1\), distinct deterministic states \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_1,\ldots,\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a tail-measurable \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\) such that \(P_{\eta_0}\{(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\to\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\}=1\) for every \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), with \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j\) if and only if the projected limit equals \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_j\). If this finite family exists, identify \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\), the projected limit states, and the initial-slope basins \(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\}\), and determine whether, for every compact \(K_0\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\operatorname{relint}_{\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j)\), there exist deterministic \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) satisfying \(\sup_{\eta_0\in K_0}P_{\eta_0}\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,2})^\top-\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\|_2>r_T(K_0)\}\le\delta_T(K_0)\). If finite projected tail selection fails, characterize the projected almost-sure limit set instead. Any ODE or stochastic-approximation reduction must be derived for the augmented chain and may not treat the slopes alone as Markov or \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) as invariant. This question concerns only the bounded-analogue dynamics and asserts neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference result must separately define \(g_{\mathrm{GX}}\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a unique \(\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a nonzero \(c_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and \(\tau_{\mathrm{GX}}=c_{\mathrm{GX}}^\top\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and must verify every class assumption.

defs.def:guoxu-dynamics-handle: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. Analyze this augmented chain on \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\): the set is invariant because an updated slope is a convex combination of its preceding value and \(Y(a)/X\), while an unupdated slope is fixed and every inverse-Gram coordinate stays in \([0,1]\). Classify projected almost-sure limit sets directly from the augmented transition kernel; any stochastic-approximation ODE used in this classification must be derived for the augmented chain. If the projected limits are finitely many isolated deterministic states, combine compact containment in relative basin interiors with a finite-cover argument to seek the common Cesaro moduli \(r_T(K_0)\) and \(\delta_T(K_0)\).
defs.def:guoxu-recursion: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and each \(\sigma_a^2\) equals the variance of the corresponding Gaussian innovation in Guo and Xu, Section 3.1. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), apply a fixed tie rule to maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

snapshot.stmt:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.

defs.def:guoxu-recursion: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and each \(\sigma_a^2\) equals the variance of the corresponding Gaussian innovation in Guo and Xu, Section 3.1. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), apply a fixed tie rule to maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

snapshot.stmt: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, \(\widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). This uniform statement strictly strengthens Saco's pointwise realized-QV pivot on the conditional finite-attractor class by deriving the variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the common attraction and exact-root localization controls.

defs.def:event-truncated-rqv-sandwich: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).
defs.def:realized-qv-pivot: For nonzero \(c\), define \(T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)/\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_Tc}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For each \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), write \(\mathcal J_P=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), \(p_{P,j}=P(J=j)\), and let \(V_{P,j}\) denote the value of \(V_j\) under \(P\). The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_P\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest label-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is the \(P\)-specific finite-mixture approximation
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), there is a subsequence \(T_\ell\to\infty\), a fixed set \(\mathcal J_0\), and limits \(p_j^\infty\) and positive-definite \(V_j^\infty\) such that \(\mathcal J_{P_{T_\ell}}=\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Along this subsequence, every fixed contrast has the centered Gaussian-mixture limit with weights \(p_j^\infty\) and projected variances \(c^\top V_j^\infty c\), omitting zero limiting weights. If two positive limiting weights have unequal projected variances, this limit is not Gaussian. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(J)\), even when all basin covariance matrices are equal.

defs.def:basin-covariance: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).
defs.def:finite-attractor-class: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\).
defs.def:ipw-z-estimator: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

assumptions.ass:iid-full-data: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-randomization: Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-overlap: For every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), context, and realized history, \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\).
assumptions.ass:bounded-score: The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:smooth-z-map: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
assumptions.ass:policy-lipschitz: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
assumptions.ass:finite-tail-selection: There is a tail variable \(J\in\mathcal J\), measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge1}\), such that \(\eta_t\to\bar\eta_J\) almost surely under \(P\).
assumptions.ass:vanishing-modulus: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).
assumptions.ass:basin-nondegeneracy: The basin covariances satisfy \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).

snapshot.stmt: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, \(\widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). This is a uniform primitive verification for the present IPW-Z finite-Cesaro-regime class: it derives the self-normalized variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the common Cesaro attraction and exact-root localization controls. It is not a literal strict tightening of Saco's pointwise AIPW/DML theorem because the estimator and hypothesis classes are different.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence or subsequence for which the \(P_\ell\)-specific mixture parameters in Theorem 1 have a fixed support \(\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_\ell,j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_\ell,j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Put \(\mathcal J_\infty=\{j\in\mathcal J_0:p_j^\infty>0\}\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if \(c^\top V_j^\infty c=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). The necessity identifies the law of the limiting finite centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it is not a one-level variance-matching claim.

Along any sequence or subsequence with limiting mixture parameters \((p_j^\infty,V_j^\infty)_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}\) as in Theorem 3, a single deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). Equivalently, the limiting selected covariance that equals \(V_j^\infty\) with probability \(p_j^\infty\) is almost surely the deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\). In the fixed-parameter special case this is equivalent to \(V_J=\Sigma\) almost surely. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.

For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.

defs.def:basin-covariance: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).
defs.def:directional-matrix-witness: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, and put \(\eta_t=\bar\eta_J=J-1\) for every \(t\ge1\).

snapshot.stmt:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.

defs.def:guoxu-dynamics-handle: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.
defs.def:guoxu-recursion: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

For each \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), write \(\mathcal J_P=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), \(p_{P,j}=P(J=j)\), and let \(V_{P,j}\) denote the value of \(V_j\) under \(P\). The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_P\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest label-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is the \(P\)-specific finite-mixture approximation
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), there is a subsequence \(T_\ell\to\infty\), a fixed set \(\mathcal J_0\), and limits \(p_j^\infty\) and positive-definite \(V_j^\infty\) such that \(\mathcal J_{P_{T_\ell}}=\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Along this subsequence, every fixed contrast has the centered Gaussian-mixture limit with weights \(p_j^\infty\) and projected variances \(c^\top V_j^\infty c\), omitting zero limiting weights. If two positive limiting weights have unequal projected variances, this limit is not Gaussian. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(J)\), even when all basin covariance matrices are equal.

defs.def:finite-attractor-class: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\). The variable \(J\) is only a finite-valued terminally measurable regime label indexing the deterministic representatives \(\bar\eta_j\) and covariance atoms \(\Omega_j\). No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) to \(\bar\eta_J\) is imposed; all path approximation is supplied by the uniform Cesaro inequality in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\).
defs.def:ipw-z-estimator: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. assumptions.ass:iid-full-data: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-randomization: Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-overlap: For every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), context, and realized history, \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\).
assumptions.ass:bounded-score: The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:smooth-z-map: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.

assumptions.ass:finite-tail-selection: The finite regime label \(J\), valued in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\).
assumptions.ass:vanishing-modulus: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).
assumptions.ass:basin-nondegeneracy: The regime covariances satisfy \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).

snapshot.stmt: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). It is not a literal strict tightening of Saco's pointwise AIPW/DML theorem because the estimator and hypothesis classes are different.

Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence or subsequence for which the \(P_\ell\)-specific mixture parameters in Theorem 1 have a fixed support \(\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_\ell,j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_\ell,j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Put \(\mathcal J_\infty=\{j\in\mathcal J_0:p_j^\infty>0\}\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if \(c^\top V_j^\infty c=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). The necessity identifies the law of the limiting finite centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it is not a one-level variance-matching claim.

Along any sequence or subsequence with limiting mixture parameters \((p_j^\infty,V_j^\infty)_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}\) as in Theorem 3, a single deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). Equivalently, the limiting selected covariance that equals \(V_j^\infty\) with probability \(p_j^\infty\) is almost surely the deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\). In the fixed-parameter special case this is equivalent to \(V_J=\Sigma\) almost surely. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.

Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). snapshot.stmt:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_\infty\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest terminal-representative-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_\infty
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_\infty\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(\eta_\infty)\), even when \(V_\infty\) is deterministic.

Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\),
\[

\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]

\[

 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]

Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.

Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.

The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_\infty\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest terminal-representative-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_\infty
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d\quad\text{almost surely}.

Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_\infty\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. snapshot.stmt:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.

Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.

For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. snapshot.stmt:
Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\),
\[

 \widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_\infty=O_P(e_T),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T).
\]
Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, and \(\widehat V_T-V_\infty=O_P(e_T)\). Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For the realized-QV interval \(I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\) in \(\mathrm{def:realized\text{-}qv\text{-}wald\text{-}interval}\), every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) satisfies
\[

 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This derives the self-normalized variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the terminal-representative Cesaro attraction and exact-root localization primitives. assumptions.ass:smooth-z-map: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
assumptions.ass:vanishing-modulus: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-overlap: For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), the policy satisfies \(\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)\ge\varepsilon\).
assumptions.ass:bounded-score: The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:policy-lipschitz: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
assumptions.ass:finite-tail-selection: There exists a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\)-valued random variable \(J\) such that \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:basin-nondegeneracy: The terminal covariance satisfies \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.

In the setting of Theorem 3, suppose the limiting covariance law has finite support \(\mu=\sum_{j=1}^r p_j\delta_{W_j}\), where \(r<\infty\), every \(p_j>0\), \(\sum_jp_j=1\), and every \(W_j\) is positive definite. For a fixed nonzero \(c\), the deterministic sandwich \(\Sigma\) has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) at every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top W_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\). The same \(\Sigma\) is valid at every level for every nonzero contrast if and only if \(W_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\).

For the predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and the estimator has the uniform linearization
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\]
Without requiring convergence of \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) to any random or deterministic matrix, uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T\),
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
\]
so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly. For the event-truncated sandwich and realized-QV statistic,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) whose basin covariance lower bound is \(\omega_-\) satisfies the predictable-QV growth condition with any strictly smaller positive growth constant. Hence its realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage, including the original truncation threshold \(\omega_-/2\), are corollaries. Saco's Theorem 5.14 is a pointwise realized-QV result for a distinct logged-propensity martingale AIPW/DML setup under variance growth; the two estimator and hypothesis classes are non-nested, and no strict theorem-level tightening is asserted.

defs.def:event-truncated-rqv-sandwich: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).
defs.def:finite-attractor-class: For fixed \(m\), \(\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\), \(s_\eta\), \(p_-\), \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T\) to be the set of laws \(P\) that, at horizon \(T\), satisfy every condition in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) with these common objects, envelopes, and moduli. The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). defs.def:ipw-z-estimator: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).
defs.def:qv-growth-ipwz-class:

\[
 \mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score},
\]
\[
 \mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}.
\]
The sequence \((\mathfrak Q_T)_{T\ge1}\), as a whole, is required to satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}predictable\text{-}qv\text{-}growth}\), with the supremum taken over the chosen subclass \(\mathfrak Q_T\) at horizon \(T\). Thus \(\mathfrak Q_T\) is not stipulated to be the maximal class of every law satisfying the pointwise base conditions. In this definition, \(r_T\) and \(\delta_T\) enter only through the numerical approximation tolerance in \(\mathrm{def:ipw\text{-}z\text{-}estimator}\); no state-attraction interpretation is imposed. Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\omega_c>0\). For the projected predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,

 =O_P(T^{-1/2})

\[

 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})

\[

 \longrightarrow0.
\]

\[

 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The full predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\) satisfies the projected condition simultaneously for all \(\|c\|_2=1\) with the common choice \(\omega_c=\omega_-/(KD_1)^2\). Thus the preceding pivot and coverage conclusions hold with an additional supremum over all unit contrasts on \(\mathfrak Q_T\). Finally, every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies the projected condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\) and every
\[
 0<\omega_c<\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2},
\]
so the same contrast-specific realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage are further corollaries.

Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\omega_c>0\). For the projected predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\) and \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) need not converge, the contrast-specific truncation is inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

\[
 0<\omega_c<\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2},
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\omega_c>0\). For the projected predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\) and \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) need not converge, the contrast-specific truncation is inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The full predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\) satisfies the projected condition simultaneously for all \(\|c\|_2=1\) with the common choice \(\omega_c=\omega_-/(KD_1)^2\). Thus the preceding pivot and coverage conclusions hold with an additional supremum over all unit contrasts on \(\mathfrak Q_T\). Finally, every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies the projected condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\) and every
\[
 0<\omega_c<\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2},
\]
so the same contrast-specific realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage are further corollaries.

defs.def:event-truncated-rqv-sandwich:
Set
\[

\]

\[

 \begin{cases}
 c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,
   &\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\
 0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,
 \end{cases}
\]

\[

\]

\[

   &\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c),\\

 \end{cases}
\]

Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]

There is a bounded two-arm, one-dimensional adaptive IPW-Z experiment targeting the causal arm-mean contrast \(\theta^*=E[Y_t(1)]-E[Y_t(2)]\), with uniform overlap and nonsingular Jacobian, for which \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\ge4\) almost surely but the realized-QV score pivot, and hence its feasible IPW-Z counterpart, has a nonstandard noncentered limit. Specifically, at horizons \(T=2n\), the limit is
\[
 L=\mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables, and
\[
 E[L]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac3{28}}-\frac1{\sqrt8}\right)\ne0.
\]
Thus a predictable-QV lower floor and realized-to-predictable QV consistency do not suffice for a Gaussian self-normalized pivot when an early score selects the later variance regime.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \((X_{T,t},\mathcal G_{T,t})_{t=1}^T\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array under \(P\), let \(0\le k_T<T\), and suppose \(|X_{T,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_T\) be \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\)-measurable and satisfy \(0<v_-\le\lambda_T\le v_+<\infty\) almost surely. If
\[
 \Delta_T:=E_P\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]-\lambda_T\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
The conclusion is uniform over any collection of arrays having common \(L,v_-,v_+\) and a common upper bound on \(\Delta_T\) that tends to zero.

Let \(0<a\le b<\infty\), and let \((U_n)\) be random symmetric \(d\)-by-\(d\) matrices satisfying \(aI_d\preceq U_n\preceq bI_d\) almost surely. There are a subsequence \((n_k)\) and a Borel probability measure \(\mu\), supported on \(\mathcal K_{a,b}=\{u=u^\top:aI_d\preceq u\preceq bI_d\}\), such that \(E[f(U_{n_k})]\to\int f(u)\,d\mu(u)\) for every continuous \(f:\mathcal K_{a,b}\to\mathbb R\).

In the setting of Theorem 3, suppose the limiting covariance law has finite support \(\mu=\sum_{j=1}^r p_j\delta_{W_j}\), where \(r<\infty\), every \(p_j>0\), \(\sum_jp_j=1\), and every \(W_j\) is positive definite. For a fixed nonzero \(c\), the deterministic sandwich \(\Sigma\) has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) at every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top W_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\). The same \(\Sigma\) is valid at every level for every nonzero contrast if and only if \(W_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\).

The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]

defs.def:ipw-z-estimator: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. snapshot.stmt:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\]
Then \(J_T\) and \(\Lambda_T\) are \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, all early-scale conditions hold uniformly, and the same pivot and coverage conclusions follow.

defs.def:event-truncated-rqv-sandwich:
Set
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\}.
\]
Define the total nonnegative scalar
\[
 \widehat q_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,
   &\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\
 0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,
 \end{cases}
\]
where the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and set
\[
 \mathcal E_T(c)=\mathcal H_T\cap\{\widehat q_T(c)\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\}.
\]
Define the total early-scale event-truncated sandwich by
\[
 \widehat V_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top},
   &\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c),\\
 I_d,&\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c)^c.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus every inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and \(c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c>0\) for every realization because \(c\ne0\).

defs.def:realized-qv-pivot:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich \(\widehat V_T(c)\) and define the everywhere finite statistic
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=
 \frac{\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)}
 {\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c}}.
\]
The denominator is positive on every realization by the construction of \(\widehat V_T(c)\).
defs.def:realized-qv-wald-interval:

\[
 I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_T-z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T},\ 
 \widehat\tau_T+z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T}\right].
\]
